sentences.text: Yutyrannus is a proceratosaurid tyrannosauroid dinosaur, a name that translates to "feathered tyrant".
This large bipedal predator reached a length of nearly 9 meters.
The holotype, which is the oldest known specimen, measured 9 meters in length and weighed an estimated 1,414 kilograms.
Three fossils found in Liaoning Province represent the largest dinosaur specimens preserving direct evidence of feathers.
A 2023 study estimated the bite force at 2,405 Newtons, which equals 540 pounds-force.
Xu Xing and colleagues named and described Yutyrannus huali in 2012.
Fossils of this animal have been found in Liaoning Province, China.
Researchers suggest the feathers may have covered the whole body to regulate temperature in a climate with an average annual temperature of 10 degrees Celsius.
A 2018 study indicates Yutyrannus had a simple hyoid structure and a flat tongue like a crocodile.
During growth, the skull became more robust and deeper.
Xu Xing speculated that Yutyrannus may have hunted sauropods based on sauropod material found in the same quarry.
Some paleontologists, including Xu Xing, suggest that Yutyrannus hunted in packs because the three known individuals were found together.
The true cause of death for the known Yutyrannus specimens remains unknown.
All phylogenetic analyses classify Yutyrannus within the group Tyrannosauroidea, and it was assigned to Tyrannosauroidea by its describers in 2012.
Yutyrannus belongs to the parent group Proceratosauridae.
Yutyrannus lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now northeastern China, specifically from the Lujiatun or Jianshangou beds of the Yixian Formation.
Age estimates suggest Yutyrannus originated from the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 125 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
The environment where Yutyrannus lived was comparable to modern temperate tropical rainforests in British Columbia and experienced significant seasonal temperature changes.
Some researchers previously hypothesized that the structures might be ancestral filamentous structures rather than true feathers.
Some paleontologists interpret Yutyrannus as a pack hunter because the three known individuals were allegedly found together.
It is debated whether the skin of later tyrannosaurids developed scales secondarily in response to body size, warmer climates, or other factors.
